note: GAMEPLAY TUNING, not historical fact. How a battle reads the campaign. Read by the sim (field strength, rounds, sieges) and by the Unreal battle (end conditions, resupply). Every value is a starting value.

field.note: A bot budget is split between the two sides in proportion to their fit soldiers, then each share is clamped. Soldiers on the field per campaign unit: soldiers_per_unit. The budget may be raised only when frame_rate_bar_bots bots hold frame_rate_bar frames a second in 3 samples of 3 at the resolution the game is normally played at (user decision 2026-11-14; -PA250FpsSample, results in PROGRESS.md).

casualties.note: A battle reports its casualties in men. The Unreal battle records killed or wounded on each event (Artillery pass 2026-11); CasualtiesFromLedger sums those. wounded_pct_of_fallen remains for sim auto_resolve_battle / split_fallen only (tests and pa250sim_tool). Men who surrendered are prisoners. The campaign takes whole units (soldiers_per_unit men) out of the ranks and keeps the men left over on the army for the next battle.

resolve.note: GAME INVENTION (Artillery pass 2026-11). Per-side Army Resolve 100 to 0. CP post deficit drains Resolve (not tickets). Casualties, officer/colours/cannon shocks drain it; a majority of posts recovers it slowly. At 0 the side breaks (end_reason army_broke). Tickets equal men: one man leaving (kia/wia/pow) spends one ticket.

rounds.note: One cartridge in a town magazine is a bundle of rounds_per_cartridge rounds. Every army carries its own rounds (Army.rounds_per_man in the save): a full box is carried_per_man. The boxes pay for what the army fires and they fill only while the army stands in a town its side holds, charged to that town's magazine, never above carried_per_man. A side fighting in a town it holds also has that magazine at hand: it opens with the magazine shared among its men when that is more than the boxes hold (up to max_per_man), and the magazine is charged for its shots before the boxes are. A column has only its boxes. No side opens with fewer than min_per_man. A beaten army that quits the field leaves defeat_drop_pct of its boxes behind, rout_drop_pct when it routed or broke (end_reason routed, army_broke), rounded up to a whole round a man; the winner's men fill their boxes from what was dropped.

siege.note: A defender beaten on its own fortified ground is besieged instead of losing the town at once.

army_broke.note: End condition: this share of a side's squads withdrawing or routing for this long. Never before min_elapsed_seconds, never against a side that fielded fewer than min_squads squads. The loser retreats with its survivors and loses morale_penalty campaign morale (an ordinary defeat costs morale.defeat).

morale.note: Campaign morale after a battle, for each army that fought in the town. victory is added to a winner. defeat is taken from a loser, unless the fight ended army_broke, which uses army_broke.morale_penalty instead. A fallen general's own hit is not here: persons rules.commander army_morale_on_fall on a loss, army_morale_on_fall_victory on a win (0, so a win does not go negative from the fall alone). Locked 2026-11-15.

posts_swept.note: End condition: one side holds every post for this long. Never before min_elapsed_seconds, and only when the enemy has held at least one post in this fight: a sweep is posts taken from, or taken back from, the enemy. A garrison that starts with every post cannot win by standing still, and a defender cannot win by raising a flag on a neutral post before the attacker arrives.

colours.note: Colours taken on the field (BattleResult.colours_captured). Each unit of carried_by_class an army brought carried one, so a side cannot lose more than that. Support is the Patriot cause's: colours the player takes raise it by support_per_capture each, his own colours lost lower it by the same.

cover.note: The fire-over stance. A man within snap_cm behind a wall, fence or field work that stops a ball at his chest and leaves his shoulder clear is down while he loads and up while he presents. Bots do it at the covered places their squad gives them; the player does it by himself when he reloads facing such cover.
cover.walls_note: GAME INVENTION (2026-11-15). Men who seek cover take places along the walls themselves: one every slot_spacing_cm, stand_off_cm back from the wall's face, on the side away from the enemy, within search_cm of a man's place in his squad, and only where the wall stands between him and the enemy: the enemy no more than max_angle_deg off the square of the wall (a man beside the end of a wall that runs toward the enemy is not behind it). A place counts only if the wall stops a ball at the chest, the shoulder is clear over it, and (once the squad is in contact) the man can see that enemy from it. before_contact: a squad HOLDING ground (its own post, its works, or ordered to take cover) takes its places fronting the enemy's side before he is in sight; a squad with somewhere to go never does. line_troops: whether squads that fire by volley use the walls too (never, holding = only a squad whose post is its own side's, always). Skirmishers (light infantry, militia) always seek cover.

works.note: Field works. A breastwork is one bank a man fires over (height between a man's chest, 90 cm, and his shoulder, 145 cm); a redoubt is three banks about a post, open to the rear. The defender's fortification_level stands breastworks_by_level[level] breastworks and redoubts_by_level[level] redoubts at the start (the last entry serves any higher level); the other places are empty and a sapper can build on them. Places are the level's PA250WorksSlot markers, or breastwork_slots places made up slot_ring_cm out from the defender's post when the level has none. A work is cover once it stands to cover_built_share of its height; health is what round shot has to batter away. Whoever defends a post mans the works within man_radius_cm of it.

smoke.note: GAME INVENTION. Powder smoke hides men from the bots (the player sees it for himself). Each puff counts as thick within sight_radius_scale of its width; when the smoke lying on a line of sight adds up to sight_block_opacity or more (0 clear, 1 solid), the man beyond it cannot be seen or fired at. One fresh puff is not enough; the bank a volley leaves is, for some seconds, until it thins and drifts.

sound.note: Gunfire is heard after it is seen: its sound reaches the player speed_m_per_second later for every metre between them (343 is the real figure). Nothing is delayed inside no_delay_within_m.

duel.note: GAME INVENTION. The shove (B): the musket held across the body and driven into a man within shove_range_cm. It does no harm; it drives him back shove_push_cm, plants him for shove_stagger_seconds and for shove_open_seconds he can neither block nor parry, so the thrust that follows goes home. The shover recovers in shove_recover_seconds and cannot shove again for shove_cooldown_seconds. Thrust, guard, parry, riposte and butt-stroke values stay in DA_MeleeTuning.

remnant.note: End condition `routed`: a side with no reserve and this few men standing quits the field after this long (never the human player's side while he is alive on it). From mark_men down, its men are marked on the enemy player's HUD so the last of them can be found.

resupply.note: A soldier inside a post his side holds refills his cartridge box from the side's pool. One full box is kept back for the human player.

modes.note: The kind of fight (BattleSetup.mode, chosen by the sim's choose_battle_mode). landing: the attacker arrived by an edge of one of landing_edge_types into a town with the landing_town_tag terrain tag; this comes first, so a fortified harbour town reached over the water is a landing. assault: otherwise, the defender's fortification level is assault_min_fort_level or more. conquest: everything else, and always for the presets in conquest_presets (the scripted North Bridge and Battle Road fights).

bridge_company.note: GAME INVENTION. At Concord (concord_bridge) only part of the British column goes down to the North Bridge; the rest waits in the town. When match_defender_units is true the company matches the provincial units on the field (never outnumbers them), so the opening fight is at least parity when the column is large enough. fallback_units is used only if the defender has no units.

assault.note: GAME INVENTION. The defender holds every post. The attacker must carry them in order, nearest his start first: only the next one can be contested, and a post he has carried stays his. Each post carried adds seconds_per_post_carried to the clock. When the clock runs out the defender has held (time_limit, the defender wins); when the attacker carries the last post the field is his (posts_swept). No reserve bleed for posts. garrison_share_pct of the defender's squads stand at the post under attack.

landing.note: GAME INVENTION. The attacker's first wave comes in by boat: up to boats boats of men_per_boat men (as many as the men on the field need) start row_out_m off the landing place and row in at boat_speed_cm a second; nobody in a boat can fire or move, and the men are free disembark_seconds after the keel touches. The boats wait up to player_wait_seconds for the player to take his place. Men beyond the first wave, and every replacement, come ashore at the landing place once the first boat is in. The post nearest the landing place is the landing post: until the attacker has held it every other post is closed to him; from then on it is the open fight for the posts. Boats land at the level's PA250BoatLanding markers, or boat_spacing_cm apart by the attacker's start when it has none.

guns.note: Field guns in the campaign (Army.guns, ProvinceStores.guns). An army brings to a battle as many of its guns as it has crews for: crew_units_per_gun units of crew_class serve one gun. An army with crews standing in a town its side holds takes the guns laid up in that magazine, as many as its crews can serve. A beaten army that quits the field leaves the guns the enemy overran (BattleResult.guns_taken); an army destroyed leaves them all.

cannon.note: The field gun in a battle (a light 3- or 6-pounder). GAME INVENTION throughout: times and ranges are shortened to the size of the field. crew_men serve one gun; with fewer than min_crew at it, it can be neither worked nor moved. The drill (sponge and load, ram home, prime and lay) takes the three *_seconds with a full crew of gunners; a short crew is slower in proportion and men who are not gunners are slower by untrained_drill_scale. Round shot flies round_shot_range_m at round_shot_speed_m a second, scatters within round_shot_spread_degrees of where the piece was laid, goes through round_shot_pierce_men men, knocks down men within knockdown_radius_cm, batters works, and puts morale_pressure for morale_seconds. Inside grape_range_m the crew fires grape: grape_balls musket balls in a cone of grape_cone_degrees. Past that, round shot out to round_shot_range_m. Shell is a timed fuse to the mark (shell_*). The crew loads shell only past round shot, and only when shell_range_m is longer than round_shot_range_m (a howitzer's reach). These numbers keep shell inside the round, so the crew never loads shell; the player still can. A chosen load past its range is refused (grape still fires a little past grape_range_m, 1.25 times). The mesh is one piece, so it stays level: elevation_* is the ballistic lay onto the aim mark, not a pitched carriage. An idle crew pushes at push_speed_cm once own men are follow_gap_m ahead. Capture and crew_radius as before. length_cm fits the purchased mesh (333 is its own length). Gun types (Battle Feel 2026-11-16, GAME INVENTION): gun_types lists the loads each kind of piece fires; default_gun_type is every piece's kind unless a battle sets another (Percy's Lexington guns are six-pounders, so no shell there). Shell fuse variance (shell_fuse_variance, a fraction of the fuse either way) and duds (shell_dud_chance: the shell flies and lands unburst) apply only to shell. A ball grazes and goes on only above bounce_min_speed_mps. The drill is Swab, Load, Ram, Run out (run_out_seconds), Prime, Fire. missing_roles_scale: a crew short of a full crew (but at least min_crew) is slower by this factor on top of the manning share (moved 1:1 from a C++ constant). Tracker 'grapeshot' is the canister load (EPA250Shot::Grape in code).

blast.note: GAME INVENTION (Artillery pass M9). Shared blast path for shell burst, premature muzzle discharge, and ammunition-chest detonation. Outer radii and impulses scale by size; outcome rings are fractions of the outer radius. Cover (LOS blocked) drops one ring. Knockdown/stagger/flinch spend no ticket. Ragdoll cap and 1.5 s settle apply only to blast knockdowns (horse throws keep their own constants). Chest ready_rounds and refill are GAME INVENTION: Load takes one from the chest; Fire spends through GunShots/magazine; chest refills near a friendly command post while the magazine holds spare rounds beyond those already in chests. chest.resolve_own is the Resolve the chest's own side loses when it blows; chest.resolve_enemy is what the other side loses, 0 since 2026-11-16 (it was 8: a side lost Resolve because its enemy's chest blew).

drill.note: Drill orders and volley timing (Battle Feel Pass, 2026-11-16). make_ready_s / present_s moved 1:1 from FVolleyTuning (DA_MusketTuning held no override of them; the struct fields are gone, so this is the only source). GAME TUNING: response_delay_s is how long men take to obey a word of command (advance = Form line, halt = Hold; fire = from the word to the first musket). volley_spread_s: every presented man of a steady line fires inside this window. While a squad has lost its officer (officer_replace_s, then a sergeant takes the file) it fires raggedly: spread x ragged_spread_scale and its stage times and order responses x ragged_response_scale. Fall in (K): the player joins the nearest friendly line within fall_in_radius_m; he falls out when he strays fall_in_break_m from his place or presses K again.
